dataRole: canonical reduced pure-substance unary model with source-formulation fits, explicit mathematical extensions, and separately identified derived verification

referenceState.name: Mutually compatible IAPWS-95 and IAPWS Ice Ih formulation reference
referenceState.energyReference: The encoded molar Gibbs energies retain the mutually compatible reference convention of IAPWS-95 and IAPWS R10-06(2009). They are not standard Gibbs energies of formation and have not been shifted to force either phase transition.

pressure.interpretation: thermodynamic pressure of pure H2O; for the pure vapor this is also p_H2O

excludedContexts: independently specified total pressure and H2O partial pressure

systemValidity.rationale: Deliberately reduced 1-atm OBGEL scope containing the Ice Ih, liquid-water, and water-vapor stable regimes. The bounds are not limits of the underlying IAPWS formulations. Complete three-branch comparison over this scope uses explicit tangent extensions for Ice Ih above its adopted model-validity endpoint and vapor below its adopted model-validity endpoint.

mathematicalConventions.segmentIntervals: Each source-fit segment includes its adopted model-validity endpoint; an adjacent tangent-extension segment excludes the shared endpoint so exactly one expression is selected within a function.
mathematicalConventions.outsideValidity: No canonical value is supplied outside systemValidity; consumer-level extrapolation must be explicit.
mathematicalConventions.coefficientInterpretation: Each Gibbs-energy expression evaluates to J/mol when T is supplied in K.
mathematicalConventions.baseFunctionSemantics: All three phase functions are independent reductions on the common IAPWS reference convention; none uses baseFunction. Function keys identify phases rather than asserting stability.

iceIh.name: gIceIhH2O
iceIh.thermodynamicRole: Ice Ih molar Gibbs-energy branch at 101325 Pa
iceIh.quantity: G(H2O,Ice Ih,T; P=101325 Pa) on the IAPWS formulation reference

metadata.modelValidityStatus: source-formulation-derived reduced fit over the adopted stable Ice Ih interval

extension.construction: first-order tangent to the fitted Ice Ih Gibbs energy at 273.1525192653757 K
extension.interpretation: Provided only so the generic reader can compare all candidate phases across systemValidity; it does not assert physical Ice Ih metastability or extend function-level model validity.

impliedHeatCapacity.status: extension-derived mathematical consequence, not a physical Ice Ih heat-capacity claim

liquid.name: gLiquidH2O
liquid.thermodynamicRole: Liquid-water molar Gibbs-energy branch at 101325 Pa
liquid.quantity: G(H2O,liquid,T; P=101325 Pa) on the IAPWS formulation reference

metadata.modelValidityStatus: source-formulation-derived reduced fit with positive-stiffness liquid roots throughout the adopted interval

sourceScopeIntervals.note: Subcooled liquid. IAPWS-95 describes this as extrapolation and notes that a separate supercooled-water guideline gives a better representation.
Superheated positive-stiffness liquid root from IAPWS-95.

vapor.name: gVaporH2O
vapor.thermodynamicRole: Water-vapor molar Gibbs-energy branch at 101325 Pa
vapor.quantity: G(H2O,vapor,T; P=101325 Pa) on the IAPWS formulation reference

metadata.modelValidityStatus: source-formulation-derived reduced fit restricted to the stable vapor branch

spinodal.interpretation: The positive-stiffness low-density IAPWS-95 root ends here. No physically or source-formulation-valid vapor branch is claimed at lower temperature.

unadoptedSourceFormulationRegion.reason: Near-spinodal heat-capacity divergence prevents a useful single compact reduction, and IAPWS cautions that the subcooled-vapor extrapolation is reasonable only close to saturation.

extension.construction: first-order tangent to the fitted stable-vapor Gibbs energy at 373.12429584768444 K
extension.interpretation: Provided only so the generic reader can compare all candidate phases across systemValidity. It replaces neither the cautioned IAPWS-95 metastable root above the spinodal nor the absent root below the spinodal, and it does not assert physical vapor metastability anywhere below the attachment temperature.

impliedHeatCapacity.status: extension-derived mathematical consequence, not a physical vapor heat-capacity claim

sourceProvenance.sourceFamily: IAPWS reference formulations reduced to the OBGEL unary temperature basis at fixed pressure

numericalImplementationAdapter.role: Numerical evaluator used to sample the published formulations; not the scientific authority.

sourceProvenance.provenanceRule: Source-formulation values, reduced-fit quantities, and extension-derived quantities remain distinct. The explicit tangent extensions are OBGEL constructions and are not attributed to IAPWS.

modelConstruction.sampling: The IAPWS formulations were sampled at 1 K spacing with exact computed phase-boundary and vapor-spinodal rows added.
modelConstruction.fittingMethod: For each candidate basis, curvature-bearing coefficients were least-squares fitted to Cp = -T d^2G/dT^2; constant and linear integration terms were then least-squares fitted to molar Gibbs energy.

selectionTargets.scope: development candidate selection only; not a repository-wide canonical acceptance standard

selectedFits.selectionNote: The five- and six-term candidates failed the heat-capacity target; adding T^-1 and T^-2 was the smallest tested basis meeting both targets.
Restricted to the supported stable vapor branch; compact fits spanning the near-spinodal metastable branch failed strongly and were rejected.

modelConstruction.transitionConstraintPolicy: Neither the source phase boundaries nor any rounded transition temperatures were imposed as fitting or stitching constraints. The encoded crossings are predictions of the independently reduced branches plus, where identified, explicit tangent extensions.
modelConstruction.metastableExtensionRule: Within systemValidity, Ice Ih above 273.1525192653757 K and vapor below 373.12429584768444 K use first-order endpoint tangents preserving G and dG/dT at the attachment temperature. These segments support comparison only and do not enlarge function-level validity.
modelConstruction.canonicalOutsideSystemExtrapolation: None. OBGEL supplies no implicit model beyond 250-500 K.

verification.reproducibilityRule: Computed values are consequences of the encoded functions and must be reproducible without using verification metadata as model input.

implementationAdapterChecks.status: passed against published IAPWS verification tables
implementationAdapterChecks.note: The individual checked quantities use their respective published units and tolerances; complete values remain in working/h2o-reduced-model/generated/h2o-fit-diagnostics.json.

iceLiquid.method: numerical root of IAPWS Ice Ih Gibbs energy minus IAPWS-95 liquid Gibbs energy at 101325 Pa

liquidVapor.method: numerical root of IAPWS-95 liquid Gibbs energy minus IAPWS-95 vapor Gibbs energy at 101325 Pa

vaporSpinodal.method: simultaneous fixed-pressure solution of P(T,rho)=101325 Pa and (partial P/partial rho)_T=0 for the low-density IAPWS-95 root

computedValue.method: numerical root of equal encoded Gibbs energies
computedValue.note: The crossing lies just above the adopted Ice Ih model-validity endpoint and therefore uses the explicit Ice Ih tangent extension. It was not imposed.

computedValue.method: numerical root of equal encoded Gibbs energies
computedValue.note: The crossing lies just below the adopted vapor model-validity endpoint and therefore uses the explicit vapor tangent extension. It was not imposed.

computedValue.method: analytical root of equal encoded linear tangent extensions, independently checked numerically
computedValue.note: Both branches use explicit tangent extensions at this temperature, and liquid is the stable lower-envelope phase. This value is not an IAPWS metastable ice-vapor equilibrium and makes no claim of physical vapor metastability beyond the spinodal.
